name: Cairngorms National Park
blurb: Pinewood, moor and arctic plateau where deer, hares and an eagle share the hills.

tip.title: Thin out the red deer
tip.text: Set Red deer to -70% and watch pine, heather and bilberry recover, hares and grouse find more food, and foxes, eagles and crows lose winter carrion.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Short, dark winters and bright summers set the growing season for plants from the glens to the high plateaux.
Moist, cool Highland weather keeps the moorland, bog and forest floor damp and supports mosses, heather and blaeberry.
Long-lying snow patches persist on the high plateaux, shaping which plants and animals can live in the arctic-alpine zone.

nodes.name: Fungi and soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead pine needles, heather, and animal remains, returning nutrients to the peaty soil.
The dominant native conifer of the Caledonian pinewood. Seedlings are often eaten by deer, which limits regrowth in many places.
Dwarf shrub that blankets the moorland. A key winter food for mountain hares, and eaten by deer and grouse.
Low shrub of the pinewood floor and moor; its leaves and berries feed deer, hares and capercaillie.
Small native tree of glens and woodland edges that bears berries and leaves taken by birds and mammals.

nodes.name: Crowberry
nodes.desc: Evergreen dwarf shrub of moor and mountain ground whose berries are eaten by grouse and capercaillie.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: Scotland's largest land mammal. Heavy grazing and browsing on heather, bilberry and young pines shapes how forest and moor regrow.

nodes.name: Roe deer
nodes.desc: Smaller deer of woodland edges that browses shrubs, heather and bilberry, and young trees.
Isolated Scottish population of the moors and hills; eats heather and, in snowy times, twigs and bark. A main prey of golden eagle and fox.
Moorland gamebird that feeds mainly on heather shoots and also on crowberry and cowberry; prey for eagles and foxes.
Lives in pine woods, where it feeds on pine seeds and other tree fruits.
Agile woodland hunter that takes squirrels, voles, birds and their eggs, as well as berries.
Generalist predator and scavenger; a major predator of mountain hares and a taker of grouse and carrion.

nodes.name: Scottish wildcat
nodes.desc: Rare forest-and-moor cat that hunts rabbits, hares, voles and birds.
Small slender hunter of voles, rabbits, hares and ground-nesting bird eggs and chicks.
Opportunist that scavenges carcasses such as winter deer carrion and also takes eggs.
Top predator of the open hills; takes hares and grouse and scavenges carrion in winter.
